edges.effect_quant: In the AMORIS cohort, increasing apoB/apoA-1 ratio showed a strong graded relationship with major adverse cardiovascular events, with a hazard ratio of 1.7 comparing the 10th versus first decile. In PCI patients, the fourth versus first apoB/apoA1 quartile carried an adjusted hazard ratio of 1.92 for future cardiovascular adverse events, and in ACS patients apoB/apoA1 independently predicted 5-year MACCE risk on top of SYNTAX severity measures.
edges.population: adults with measured apolipoproteins in primary-prevention, coronary-disease, or acute-coronary-syndrome cohorts
edges.mechanism: The apoB/apoA1 ratio captures the balance between atherogenic particle number and the anti-atherogenic HDL-associated apoA1 pool. When the ratio is high, the vascular environment is shifted toward lipoprotein retention, foam-cell formation, and plaque instability rather than cholesterol efflux and repair.
edges.summary: This is one of the more practical ratio biomarkers because it consistently outperforms intuition based on LDL cholesterol alone. Across both large population cohorts and higher-risk coronary cohorts, a higher apoB/apoA1 ratio marks people who go on to have more major cardiovascular events and to have them earlier.
edges.caveats: Thresholds vary across sex, assay, and background treatment, so this edge is better treated as a graded risk marker than a universal cutoff rule. Much of the strongest evidence is cohort-based rather than randomized biomarker-guided intervention data.
